title: Claude Personal Assistant — Logs & Traces
description: The narrative signals: every log line the hand-written Logback -> OpenTelemetry appender exports to Loki, and the traces Tempo received for the same requests. It exists so a broken export path is visible on a dashboard instead of only in an Explore search nobody ran. It charts no Prometheus metric at all — rates, latencies and counters live on the Modules and JVM & HTTP dashboards — and it deliberately shows no per-chat or per-conversation breakdown, because service_name is Loki's only index label here and promoting a chat id to a label would create one Loki stream per conversation forever.

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: A textbox, not a label_values() query like the other two dashboards use. A Loki label query returns nothing until the first log line is ingested, and Loki rejects a stream selector whose every matcher is empty-compatible ({service_name=~""}) with an error rather than an empty result — so a query variable would turn a quiet stack into a red dashboard. The value is resource attribute service.name, which the OTLP ingest path flattens to the service_name index label.

panels.title: Application log
panels.description: The reason this dashboard exists: the other two are twenty Prometheus panels and render no log line at all, so the hand-written Logback -> OpenTelemetry appender (audit/logging/) could stop exporting and nothing on any dashboard would change — the failure would only surface as an empty Explore search nobody ran. An empty panel here is a visible regression. enableLogDetails is on because the structured facts every log.atInfo().addKeyValue(...) call attaches arrive as structured metadata, and the row detail view is where they are readable.

panels.title: Error log rate
panels.description: detected_level is NOT an index label. service_name is the only one this stack has — GET /loki/api/v1/labels answers ["service_name"] — and detected_level is structured metadata like every other addKeyValue fact, however label-like it looks in a result's stream map. That is exactly why the level filter sits AFTER the {service_name="$service"} stream selector: a pipeline stage can match structured metadata, a stream selector cannot, so {detected_level="error"} would select no stream and silently return nothing. Deliberately a rate rather than a count: it stays comparable when the dashboard's time range changes, which is how the panel beside the Prometheus error meters is meant to be read.

panels.title: Tool invocation log
panels.description: The shape to copy for anything this application logs. service_name is the ONLY index label — GET /loki/api/v1/labels answers ["service_name"] and nothing else. detected_level, trace_id, span_id, tool, outcome, chatId and every other log.atInfo().addKeyValue(...) fact are STRUCTURED METADATA: they show up inside a result's stream map, which is what makes them look like labels, but no selector can match them. So the filter must sit AFTER the stream selector, as a pipeline stage ({service_name="$service"} | tool != ""), never inside it — {tool="x"} selects no stream and returns nothing, which reads as "the tool never ran" instead of "that is not a label".

panels.title: Recent traces
panels.description: Tempo's side of the same regression: sampling is pinned to 1.0 in observability.properties precisely so every turn is traceable, and until this panel existed nothing outside Explore proved a single span had arrived. Matching on resource.service.name rather than a span name keeps the panel meaningful when spans are renamed. Click a trace id to open the span view; the Loki datasource's derived trace_id field pivots the other way, from a log line into the same trace.
